item.title: Chinese navy hospital ship arrives in Senegal for medical mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
The Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy hospital ship Auspicious Ark docks in Dakar, Senegal, Sept. 25, 2026. The hospital ship arrived in Dakar, the capital of Senegal, on Friday to begin a friendly visit and provide medical services, marking the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to Senegal. (Xinhua/Qi Qi) DAKAR, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy hospital ship Auspicious Ark arrived in Dakar, the capital of Senegal, on Friday to begin a friendly visit and provide medical services, marking the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to Senegal. The hospital ship, which is carrying out Mission Harmony-2026, docked at the Port of Dakar at around 11:00 a.m. local time. Senegalese military and government officials, representatives of military personnel, the defense attache at the Chinese Embassy in Senegal and embassy staff, local residents, and representatives of the Chinese community and Chinese enterprises welcomed the ship at the port. Senegalese military and government officials, the Chinese defense attache and embassy staff then boarded the hospital ship, where they toured the vessel and held talks with representatives of the mission personnel. During the visit, the hospital ship will provide medical services aboard the vessel and send medical training personnel for hospital visits and exchanges. The mission will also organize a deck reception, visit a local orphanage and hold a friendly basketball match with Senegalese military personnel.

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to high-level dialogue marking 5th anniversary of GDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) held at the UN headquarters in New York on Friday. Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind, Xi said. Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted. Xi pointed out that nowadays, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and people in all countries are more keen about development. As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said.

item.title: China, U.S. agree on constructive strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan have a chat over tea with U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The consensus was reached during a tea chat at the White House attended by Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, and Trump and his wife, Melania Trump. Xi said the trip to Washington was his first state visit to the United States in 11 years. During the visit, the two sides added new substance to the vision for the China-U.S. relationship, and agreed to jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Xi said. The two sides also achieved mutually beneficial outcomes in the economic and trade fields, which will be welcomed by the people of both countries and the international community, he added. Stressing that the future of China-U.S. relations is bright, Xi said that it reflects the trend of history. The road to a bright future is often winding, with difficulties and challenges bound to arise along the way, Xi said, adding that it is in line with the laws governing the development of things. Xi said he is willing to work with Trump to write a new chapter in the history of China-U.S. relations with the courage and a sense of responsibility to history. Calling Xi's state visit to the United States constructive and very successful, Trump said that the two sides held in-depth exchanges on U.S.-China relations and major international and regional issues, achieving positive outcomes that will benefit both countries. He said he looks forward to maintaining close contact with Xi and jointly guiding the development of U.S.-China relations. After the tea chat, Xi and Peng, accompanied by Trump and Melania, visited the U.S. National Archives. They walked together into the central hall, where they were briefed on the National Archives and its exhibits. The archives carry the wisdom of the forebears and offer insights for the future, Xi said, adding that over the past 250 years, the American people have pursued the American Dream and built a prosperous country and a beautiful home on the North American continent. The Chinese people, inheriting 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, have continued to make new achievements on the new journey toward realizing the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. As two distinctive countries, China and the United States have different histories and cultures, social systems and development paths, Xi said. However, the people of the two countries share the same aspiration for a better life despite the differences, he said. If the two countries recognize and respect their differences, deepen mutual understanding and learn from each other, seek the biggest common denominator, expand the list of areas for cooperation, and properly manage differences, China-U.S. relations will enjoy steady and sustained growth, Xi said. item.title: Japan Should Stop Sowing Discord in the South China Sea: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- "We urge the Japanese side to offer a clear explanation of its accelerating 'remilitarization' efforts, and stop sowing discord and undermining peace and stability in the South China Sea," said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, at a press conference on Thursday. In the wake of the incident provoked by a Philippine government vessel near Xianbin Jiao of China's Nansha Qundao, the Japanese Embassy in the Philippines quickly posted on social media that it's "gravely concerned" over the "dangerous actions" by China, and portrayed itself as "upholding the rule of law and opposing any actions which increase tensions". In response, the spokesperson pointed out that it's clear and evident that the Philippine government vessel made provocations near Xianbin Jiao and deliberately rammed a China Coast Guard vessel. Though Japan is not a country directly involved in the South China Sea issue, it has actively joined the Philippine side in distorting facts.The real intention is to make waves in the South China Sea and fish in muddy waters. The spokesperson then emphasized that the Chinese side firmly opposes this behavior. He added that the Japanese side has been strengthening its collusion with the Philippines by providing weapons and sending troops to the Philippines for joint exercises, during which it launched offensive missiles overseas for the first time. "The Japanese side is attempting to break away from the post-war international order and revive its old dream of military expansion. This is a real threat to regional peace and stability," stressed the spokesperson.

item.title: China urges Japan to draw lessons from history, win trust through concrete actions: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- China on Wednesday urged Japan to draw lessons from history, deeply reflect on the past, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked to comment on Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's speech at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, in which she said that Japan is a peace-loving country and called for the deletion of the "enemy state clauses" from the UN Charter. "Compared with what Japan says, the international community is more concerned about what Japan does," Guo said. He said post-war Japan's concept of being a "peace-loving country" was built on deeply reflecting on its history and making a complete break with militarism. "In fact, the current Japanese administration not only denies its history of aggression and whitewashes its war crimes, but also continues to build up its military and expand its armaments, accelerates 'remilitarization,' seeks to abandon the Three Non-Nuclear Principles and revise the pacifist Constitution, and openly challenges the post-war international order," Guo said. Japan has become a prominent factor threatening regional peace and stability, he stressed. This year marks the 81st anniversary of the founding of the United Nations and the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trial, Guo said, adding that Japan joined the UN on the premise of acknowledging the crimes of militarism and accepting the UN Charter in its entirety. The "enemy state clauses" in the UN Charter constitute important institutional arrangements aimed at preventing fascism and militarism from once again threatening international peace and security, and provide important institutional safeguards for upholding the post-war international order, Guo said. "To this day, they still carry important practical significance," he said. "We urge the Japanese side to draw lessons from history, deeply reflect on the past, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions," Guo said.
